title: Tracepod profile document (schema v4)
description: The profile JSON the sensor writes to profiles/<container-id>/files.json (standalone mode) or POSTs to the controller (DaemonSet mode). One document per container profiling window. v4 adds the "s" access mode (stat-family existence checks, emitted only when the sensor runs with --trace-stat) and the "inferred-runtime" observation source (build-time runtime companion rules) on top of v3; no v3 field semantics changed. See docs/profile-schema/README.md for the versioning policy and field semantics.

schema_version.description: Profile schema version. Always the integer 4 for documents matching this schema. A legacy pre-versioned profile carries the string "1" (or no field) and must be treated as v1.

container_id.description: Runtime container ID the sensor profiled.

image_ref.description: OCI image reference of the profiled container. Omitted in standalone mode when no image ref was resolved.

profile_start.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp when the aggregator was created (first witnessed start).

profile_end.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp when the profile was snapshotted (container stop).

coverage.description: Per-container coverage markers (R2). The sensor records raw signals; it does not score them.

process_start_observed.description: True only when the sensor can demonstrate it observed the container's main process from its first exec (its cgroup attachment won the NRI startup race). Any uncertainty resolves to false. A false value means startup code paths are systematically missing from this profile.

attach_time.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp when the sensor added the container's cgroup to the BPF allowlist — the earliest instant any event could be observed. The zero value (0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) means no attach was recorded.

first_exec_time.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the first exec event observed for the container. Omitted when no exec was observed during the window.

container_starts.description: Container starts the sensor witnessed during the window (R3), in observation order. A consumer counts full restarts within a profile as length-1, summing across the profiles emitted for a workload for cross-window totals.

timestamp.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the witnessed start.

event_loss.description: Window-level event-loss counters (v3). Counts are process-wide and per profiling window, NOT per container: buffer drops are not attributable to one container, so any nonzero total taints 'not observed => not loaded' conclusions for every container observed in this window. total counts HARD losses only and is a strict-zero gate: total==0 is a positive claim ('instrumented at every audited hard loss point and lost nothing'), never 'did not count'. Tolerated losses (counted observations lost with a known intrinsic floor) are reported separately in 'tolerated' and excluded from total; consumers MUST gate them with their own configurable ceiling and surface the counts, never fold them into total. v3 was revised in place to add 'tolerated' before any consumer existed — see docs/profile-schema/README.md (v3-revision note).

total.description: Sum of all by_stage (HARD-loss) counts; excludes tolerated. The strict-zero consumer gate: treat any nonzero value as grounds to withhold a 'never loaded' claim for the whole window.

by_stage.description: Per-stage HARD-loss counts for the window, keyed by audited loss-point name (bpf_reserve_failed, decode_failed, untracked_cgroup). Their values sum to total. A stage present with value 0 is an explicit 'counted, lost nothing'. A stage that could not be instrumented is absent here and listed in not_instrumented instead, never read as a false zero. Diagnosis only — gate on total.

tolerated.description: Per-stage TOLERATED-loss counts for the window, keyed by audited loss-point name (path_read_failed). Counted observations lost for reasons with a known intrinsic floor (e.g. an openat filename pointer that faulted before its page was present, idle floor 0-2 per container). EXCLUDED from total. A consumer MUST gate these with its own conservative, configurable ceiling and MUST surface the counts in any evidence it emits — never fold them into total, never ignore them. A stage present with value 0 is an explicit 'counted, lost nothing'.

not_instrumented.description: Audited loss points (hard or tolerated) that were NOT counted for this window (the zero-is-a-claim escape hatch). Stages named here are absent from by_stage and tolerated so they never masquerade as a zero. Empty in the normal fully-instrumented case (this sensor instruments every audited point as of v3).

files.description: Observed files, keyed by absolute path.

source.description: How the file entered the manifest. Load-bearing for confidence scoring and audit trails.

access_modes.description: Observed access modes: r (read), w (write), x (execute), l (link), m (mmap PROT_EXEC), s (stat-family existence check; --trace-stat only).

count.description: Number of observed opens. 0 for inferred-elf and directory-inclusion entries.

inferred_from.description: source=inferred-elf: the ELF binary that required this shared object. source=inferred-runtime: the observed file that implied this one (e.g. the __pycache__ pyc whose sibling .py source was added).

included_because.description: source=directory-inclusion / manual: the reason the path was included.
